target_customer: Research and clinical genomics labs using short read sequencers
problem: Short read sequencers cannot resolve long range information; long read platforms are expensive.
business_model: Sample preparation kits and sequencing services that turn short read machines into long read

founders.name: Tuval Ben-Yehezkel
founders.background_notes: Joined Element Biosciences as Senior Director of Applications after the acquisition

technical_complexity.rationale: Barcoding chemistry and assembly of long reads from short reads, requiring molecular biology and bioinformatics.

defensibility.rationale: Proprietary chemistry, but Illumina's synthetic long read kit and PacBio and Nanopore covered similar needs.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Element Biosciences, a sequencer maker, bought Loop in February 2022 to offer long read applications on its platform.

market_need_then: Not independently sourced for 2016; GenomeWeb described demand for long reads with molecule counting for rRNA sequencing.

rebrands.why: Element acquired Loop and kept the LoopSeq name for kits on its AVITI system; one directory claims it was later dropped, unconfirmed.

brand_strength.rationale: Little brand press; the LoopSeq name survived the acquisition for a time.

outcome_analysis: Loop Genomics developed chemistry to get long reads from short read sequencers, closed an 8M Series A reported around 2019 and was acquired by Element Biosciences in February 2022 for undisclosed terms. The founder moved into Element's applications team. With few verifiable rounds and no price, it is a technology acquisition by a sequencer company rather than a measurable venture return.
notes: Series A date conflicts (one source May 2019, CB Insights Feb 2018); investors Khosla, Fusion Fund, DN Capital come from Dealroom only and are unverified. Totals 8.1M to 10.8M vary by aggregator. The company has no website listed. Competitor snippets (Illumina TruSeq SLR, 10x, PacBio, Nanopore) were not date-verifiable to 2016, so the list is empty. Founder education not on YC page.
